text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Amsterdam Exchanges AEX plans to quote listings only in euros from the beginning of 1999. (p1)
- Philips Electronics names former Grundig chairman Pieter van der Wal head of its Southeast Asia operations. (p1)
- Dutch pension funds book an average of 15.2 pct return on investment in 1996, half a percent higher than in 1995. (p1)
- Pig breeders in the south of the Netherlands fiercely oppose ban on breeding as measure against swine fever. (p1)
- Low interest rates threaten the market for single-premium assurance. (p1)
- Pharmaceutical wholesaler group OPG and five Belgian rivals to cooperate in selling generic medicines in Belgium. (p3)
- Gist-Brocades in Peruvian joint venture for semi-synthetic penicillins. (p3)
- Van Dorp office supplies and medical disposables, is to concentrate on its core activities the import and wholesale of office supplies and agendas. (p4) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Agricultural minister Jozias van Aartsen orders all new- born pigs in swine fever area to be slaughtered. (p1)
- Cancellation of trade mission to China leaves businesses cold. (p1)
- Vision Software takes KPN to court over its use of the name Vision Networks. (p2)
- Philips Electronics stands to make millions of guilders from licences of digital video disc (DVD) players. (p33) DE TELEGRAAF
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm vexed by social affairs minister Ad Melkert's budget demands. (p7)
- Entertainment group Endemol stands to lose on the German TV market. (p10)
- Economic affairs minister Hans Wijers gives up all hope of aircraft maker Fokker's restart. (p35)
- ABN Amro the first bank to issue a bank bond in euros. (p37) TROUW
- Traffic minister Annemarie Jorritsma denies having given order for parallel runway study for Schiphol airport. (p1)
- Labour party in province of Drenthe offers to be mediator in strike at Philips plant in Hoogeveen. (p7) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Food and detergent group Unilever is considering tighter supervision on code of conduct. (p10)
- Bad stocking up costs Dutch supermarkets 1.5 bn guilders turnover a year. (p10)
